digest.component_or_area: LLM gate cost analysis and lever evaluation
propositions: Per-gate LLM costs since Bedrock switch are: plan-review 3.02 dollars, code-review 1.42 dollars, completion-verifier 2.24 dollars; mean per-ticket cost 11.85 dollars.

Cheap-model experiments (Nova Pro, Haiku, Nova 2 Lite) rejected Haiku for agentic review and Nova Pro for completion verification due to false-accept rates, retained Sonnet for CV, identified Nova Pro at 30-40x cost reduction as frontier slot candidate bounded by ~50-57% blocking-criteria recall.

Code-review severity axes are inert not because findings are rare but because blocking is routed (98.2% of findings have blocking_enabled=False) and the 0.95 threshold is unreachable (only 0 of 3,738 gradings achieved the required 3-way AND of blast_radius=system AND likelihood=high AND reversibility=hard).

Ordinal migration plan (Phases 0-3) requires operator approval before execution; Phase 0 removes unused base-five emissions, Phase 1-2 convert to deterministic kind sets and binary subquestions, Phase 3 addresses code-review separately using 3,230-finding verification corpus.

Deprecation removal readiness found nothing with met removal condition; only gitattributes migration arm (item 1, ~15 LOC) is dead and safely removable; single-pass review surfaces and REBAR_LLM_MODEL are candidates for next pre-1.0 breaking window.

AWS alarm sweep identified 3 true-positive review-interrupt bound-exceeded firings (suggesting DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX undersized) and 2 false-positive defects in observability.sh probe counting (widespread-zealous-narwhal for cold-start seeding, colossal-slothful-grouse for over-broad pattern matching).
